notes.send_advice: The wording needs no change. Send it as a small name correction and say in the message that his point stands, because Microsoft runs exactly the kind of programs he describes at Mount Pleasant.
notes.reason: The live page shows the sentence outside any block quote: Zvi quotes PoliMath's complaint that a tech company spends ten billion dollars on a data center outside a Wisconsin town but will not sponsor a little league team, then answers in his own voice, 'Actually, they do this. Meta and Google have such programs. Meta has such a program at Mount Pleasant.' There is no hyperlink on that sentence, and PoliMath's article names no town, so the Mount Pleasant example is Zvi's own. The note is correct: Meta's own list of United States data centers has twenty-eight sites, none in Mount Pleasant, and its Wisconsin site is Beaver Dam; the Mount Pleasant campus is Microsoft's Fairwater facility, and Microsoft funds the Lamparek Creek restoration with Root-Pike WIN and works with Gateway Technical College on training, as the note says. What keeps this from good is that the error does not touch the argument. A data center operator really does run such community programs at Mount Pleasant, just Microsoft rather than Meta, so a reader who believes the sentence is wrong only about which company. It is the kind of one-word correction Zvi runs without complaint, but it is a name mix-up, not a broken point.
